row.evidence: Box documents no SCIM endpoint; its SSO guide says IdPs such as Okta and OneLogin integrate 'to Box through the Box API' for pre-provisioning, deprovisioning and push groups, and Microsoft's tutorial connects Entra to 'Box's user account provisioning API'.
row.notes: Status changed from gated (June) to none under the post-pilot rule for provisioning without SCIM: Box publishes no SCIM endpoint in its admin docs, developer guides or API reference (sitemaps and llms.txt indexes searched), and IdP provisioning (Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace) runs through IdP-built connectors on the proprietary Box Users/Groups API, so api_provisioning is true. The June claim that Business ($15/u/mo) is the 'SCIM plan' has no first-party source and is dropped; the only plan gate for IdP provisioning is Microsoft's and JumpCloud's 'Box Business plan' prerequisite. Prices unchanged since June: Business Starter $5, Business $15, Business Plus $25, Enterprise $35 per user/month billed annually, Enterprise Plus $50, all with a 3-user minimum; Enterprise Advanced is Contact us. The comparison table shows 'Active directory & SSO' on Business and above; whether Business Starter includes SAML is not stated. Okta's catalogue tags the Box app with SCIM although Box documents only its REST API (see conflicts).

okta.notes: Okta catalogue lists SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push; Box says Okta integrates through the Box API.

google.notes: Google's article does not name the protocol; classified api_connector because Box documents no SCIM endpoint.

onelogin.notes: Box's SSO guide gives OneLogin setup steps and says OneLogin has 'various levels of integration' through the Box API; OneLogin's own page not loaded (blocks bots).

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud's article documents SAML SSO with JIT provisioning only.

fallbacks.other_sync: SAML group sync on login (SSO Groups); IdP-built API connectors for Okta, Entra and Google Workspace

conflicts.text: Okta's catalogue page tags the Box integration with SCIM, while Box's own SSO guide says IdPs integrate through the Box API and Box documents no SCIM endpoint; Microsoft likewise calls it 'Box's user account provisioning API'.

searched: support.box.com community post 'Box API is SCIM' (login required)
open_questions: Does Business Starter include SAML SSO or REST API access? The pricing card lists neither, and the SSO article says only 'Business and Enterprise accounts'.
Which plans include the enterprise event stream (admin_logs) API is not stated.
Box does not document what an IdP deactivation does (inactive status vs delete) or whether it frees a seat; Google's article says suspension marks the Box user deactivated.
OneLogin's Box connector page was not loaded (bot protection), so OneLogin provisioning is unverified.
Whether deleting a user frees a seat: Box says deletion 'does not change the number of paid seat licenses' (seat count is unchanged; reuse of the freed seat is implied but not stated).
